svg.text: left: how a channel's number becomes spikes and zone activity; right: what the main network chooses
One channel through the analyzer (example: touch_head)
+ ON cell (value rising) and OFF cell (falling): a touch onset fires at once
habituation: each neuron of a zone tires with its own time constant, so a steady stimulus fades (1 s .. 90 s) and a new one stands out
recurrent pool, 80 / 20 excitatory / inhibitory (Dale's law), 12 % connections: context - touch while it is loud, shake after a touch ...
12 x 8 map; a bump where motion / a new bright spot is seen
-> att_x, att_y, att_strength (the eyes and the head follow it)
32 leaky integrators read all 768 neurons: smooth numbers for the main network
core affect: valence (pleasant .. unpleasant), arousal (calm .. excited),
under / over (too little / too much happening: the inverted U of Wundt and Berlyne),
threat, surprise. salience: how much a channel matters now; hedonic: is it nice.
the SNN gets only numbers and knows which channel each comes from; it does not choose emotions
pushed by 8 of the SNN's moods
bored of its own ideas (90 s);
the night learns one bias per idea
pattern: steady, breathe, pulse, flicker, wave
mode: hold, look, scan, nod, shake,
gesture library (the executor plays it on the network's wish)
SNN: an innate appraisal (teacher_snn.py) turns channel histories into the 32 numbers; the SNN learns to reproduce them from its own spikes
(surrogate gradients, TBPTT; the last 30 % of the epochs with int8 fake quantisation, as on the robot).
Data: 1400 synthetic 5-minute lives (quiet nights, play, being alone, rough handling) + 400 slices of the real diary.
NN: a behaviour teacher with memory (teacher_nn.py) acts on the SNN's numbers and the network imitates it; then DAgger: the network acts, its own choices
feed back into its inputs and the teacher labels the states it really visits. Emotion agreement acting alone: 0.84 (real lives 0.82), three DAgger rounds since the Muse.
Checks: C++ on the robot gives the same numbers as PyTorch (parity tests); simulator behaviour tests: every touch answered, petting is not annoying,
pokes are, nights are silent, play shows many faces, a lonely robot talks, shakes and claps frighten.

Life (stage 6): every night the action heads are fine-tuned on the robot's real days with AWR, rewarded by how people answered; the zones of the environment channels shift by experience; the Muse's idea biases follow what was answered.
